idea: Probabilistic structures save memory by allowing specific errors. A Bloom filter may return a false positive; a Count-Min Sketch may overestimate frequency.
steps: Hash inserts into a shared bitset and several counter rows.
Check queries against both structures and exact ground truth.
Measure false positives, occupancy and estimated frequency error.
example: A Bloom answer of absent is definitive after insert-only updates; maybe present requires an exact lookup.
concepts: Inserted keys cannot become false negatives without deletion or corruption.
Nonnegative updates mean sketch estimates cannot undercount.
The standard FPR formula is an approximation, not a guarantee on this query sample.
question: Can I delete a key by clearing its Bloom bits?
answer: No. Other keys can share those bits, so clearing them can introduce false negatives. A counting filter is a different structure.
challenge: Use Collision pressure and compare actual counts against estimates.
cost: Insert/query O(k + depth), bit memory O(m), counter memory O(width×depth); exact counts are instrumentation only.
